novelty_basis: Cusenza et al. (2022) give the exact length only for n = F_k - 1 (their Thm 1.4) and a bound otherwise; Cheigh et al. (2025) state that a closed form for non-Fibonacci inputs is open and describe the Fibonacci case as treated by Cusenza et al., whose paper we read in full and which treats F_k - 1, not F_k. The sequence L(F_k) is not in the OEIS (EXP-C19-04). Medium-low confidence that no formula exists in the literature.
proof_check: written proof (proofs/paper/C19.md Theorem 4) from CLM-C19-01, CLM-C19-02 and the published optimality of the split-first strategy (Cusenza et al. 2022, Thm 1.2); the weight sums are Lean-verified (weight_even, weight_odd, quarter_square_even, quarter_square_odd); checked for every level j <= 33 (EXP-C19-03) and by exhaustive search for n <= 150 (EXP-C19-01); awaiting independent skeptic review
statement:
With F_1 = 1, F_2 = 2, F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}, the longest Zeckendorf game on n = F_k has length
F_{k+2} - k - 2 - floor((k-1)^2/4) (0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 37, 67, 117, 201, ...), i.e. its deficit to the bound
B(F_k) is the quarter-square floor((k-1)^2/4).
title: Closed form of the longest game on a Fibonacci number: L(F_k) = F_{k+2} - k - 2 - floor((k-1)^2/4)
